method: Independently viewed all24 full native seam segments, all9 900px junctions,8 actual core-only neighbor strips and1 specific course-turn crop; additionally viewed p03_04 native+anchored guide and gold detail. Overview used for context only. No image generation, art mutation, active-map change or progress update.

findings.description: Actual north core corner/grout is near x1234 immediately above y0. Child corner begins near x1325 at y0, approximately91px rightward, creating two flat-ended parallel vertical features at the tile boundary. This confirms the previously recorded native p01_02 watch. Keep north core immutable.

Old core diagonal projecting coping arrives at boundary around y105..205; child begins plain wall with no corresponding projecting band. Several old slab divisions terminate against unmatched child masonry. This is structural mismatch, not only grain change.

Old diagonal lower coping reaches x0 around y2800, while child coping top begins around y2630. About170px height mismatch creates disconnected ledge silhouette and face. Actual old/current4096 cores used; context halo is not authority.

At lower join, the same apparent sloping band abruptly switches from old gold to child grey stone. Gold scroll is mostly inside old core and foliage obscures parts, so no separate claim that scroll shape was chopped off. Preserve this narrower material finding.

Old right-return slab grid and fine warm crosshatch differ substantially from child steep diagonal slabs and grey organic grain. Repair planning should reconcile the whole child west strip together with W01/W02 instead of treating only two endpoint pixels.

Two right side-wall projecting stone bands end at the return-wall edge near x3290, upper around y2160 and lower around y2780. The corresponding front/return projecting belts are lower, around y2330..2460 and y3000..3150, leaving a height offset rather than a continuous wrapped belt. No raster seam gap, but architecture connection is unresolved. Upper side band was already in p03_04 top anchor; compare both courses and fixed upper source before local repair. Do not assume a one-pixel blend can resolve it.

Under front projecting course, a uniform darker rectangular band ends on a perfectly straight line near y1139; start near x2000 differs from adjacent less-defined shadow. Keep as visible lighting/finish discontinuity, not a stone topology failure.
